chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessed is the obscure servant whom Allah knows but whom people do not know. They are the lanterns of guidance and the fountains of knowledge. Every dark trial is cleared away for them. They are not the broadcasters of their knowledge, nor are they the quarrelsome show-offs.'

key_terms.الْمَذَايِيعِ: Broadcasters or those who spread (knowledge widely)
key_terms.الْمُرَاءِينَ: Show-offs or those who perform for public recognition
key_terms.طُوبَى: Blessedness or happiness, often referring to a tree in Paradise
key_terms.نُوَمَةٍ: Obscure, hidden, or unknown (to the public)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the obscure servant in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s chapter on Concealment (al-Ghaybah), this hadith highlights the spiritual status of the learned who remain unrecognized by the masses, a concept often linked to the Hidden Imam and the broader community of scholars. It distinguishes them from 'al-madha'ib' (those who sell their knowledge for worldly gain) and 'al-jufat' (the ostentatious), emphasizing that true guidance comes from those whose wisdom is known to Allah but concealed from public scrutiny. This serves as a theological foundation for the value of quiet, authentic scholarship amidst social and political turmoil.
